summary: Players use a rondel to select actions each turn, researching and combining engines and bodies to build a competitive lineup of cars, then cash in on sales and race prestige. It's a tight, plan-ahead economic game where the rondel forces you to sequence actions efficiently rather than freely picking whatever you want.
praised: Satisfying engine/body combination puzzle for building cars
This edition trims luck and streamlines the fiddly original
Good component quality and thematic car-building feel
criticised: Rondel can feel restrictive or fiddly to learn at first
Racing element is a smaller, sometimes underwhelming part of the game
Can run long and a bit dry/mechanical for a car-racing theme
Niche reimplementation with less table presence than flashier economic games

interaction.kind: indirect competition over shared rondel spaces and market/race positions

scoring.why: Points come mainly from selling well-designed cars and race results, with prestige/money conversions layered on top
